verdict.headline: Retail miss and Broadcom VMware exploit pull S&P from record; small caps reach new highs
verdict.label: Data double miss stalls large caps; AVGO extends altitude ceiling; Russell 2000 closes at a record
verdict.rationale_short: The morning brief's 'binary-free' read was wrong: retail sales (−0.6% MoM) and UMich sentiment (51.0 vs 54.5) both missed, pulling the S&P −0.17% from its record while AMD's $490 close validated the AMAT China signal as equipment-specific. AVGO fell 4.1% on VMware exploitation and AI concentration — a third altitude ceiling data point, distinct from the AMAT China story. The 30Y auction stop-through at 5.22% is the first confirmed demand signal at current yield levels; Jackson Hole remains the primary venue for resolving compression or re-anchoring.

trade_setups.thesis: AVGO closed at $389.79 between $380 structural support and $400 new resistance, compressed by VMware CVE-2026-59310 exploitation liability and AI revenue concentration concerns ahead of September earnings.
trade_setups.entry: $380 is structural support below; $400 is now resistance after the 4.1% session decline. The two levels define the current range.
trade_setups.invalidation: VMware issue contained with no additional exploitation headlines in the next five sessions; stock recovers above $400 before September earnings without a guide revision.

trade_setups.thesis: The $25B 30Y auction stop-through at 5.22% (2bps below 5.24% secondary) is the first confirmed demand signal at current yield levels after three consecutive soft inflation prints. The 5.15% compression target is 7bps away.
trade_setups.entry: 5.22% is the confirmed demand level; 5.15% is the de-escalation target cited across prior briefings. 5.28% is the re-anchoring level that removes the compression thesis.
trade_setups.invalidation: 30Y closes above 5.28% before Jackson Hole on no new data — confirms market is absorbing, not pricing further compression.
trade_setups.horizon: Jackson Hole August 27-29 is the next catalyst

trade_setups.thesis: RDDT at $178.09 heading into Monday's mechanical S&P 500 inclusion auction. The August 17 closing auction concentrates passive buying; the post-inclusion sessions test whether fundamental demand — advertising durability in an AI-search environment — supports the price.
trade_setups.entry: $177 is the level that defines the fundamental bid test; $158 (pre-announcement close) is the reversion level that would indicate the pop was mechanical only.
trade_setups.invalidation: RDDT holds above $177 for two sessions after August 18 — fundamental demand present. Falls below $158 within two sessions — mechanical pop only.

bear_case: The retail sales and UMich misses are not the soft patch the equity market is pricing — they are the consumer dimension of a stagflationary backdrop where oil-driven supply inflation (WTI $82.37, Brent $88.38, SPR at 40-year lows) prevents the Fed from accommodating the growth slowdown. The UMich short-term inflation expectations spike (+11% of respondents citing Middle East and energy) arriving simultaneously with weak demand is the worst combination for the 30Y: the bond market will not compress below 5.15% if consumers are pricing more inflation even as spending softens. The altitude ceiling has three sector confirmations entering NVDA's August 26 print — CSCO (networking), AMAT (semiconductor equipment), and AVGO (networking silicon) — and all three delivered results at or above estimates before declining. If SPX cannot hold 7,700 through NVDA's result, the 7,799 record close was the cycle high.
